newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MATCH ANALYSIS OF CHELSEA V WIMBLEDON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MATCH ANALYSIS OF CHELSEA V WIMBLEDON.

text.p: Following is an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of Chelsea and Wimbledon who meet in an F.A. Cup semifinal at Highbury on Sunday (1400 GMT).

Playing style: England manager Glenn Hoddle introduced wingbacks to Chelsea during his spell as player-manager and Ruud Gullit has carried on where Hoddle left off. Dan Petrescu and Scott Minto play the wide roles with Frenchman Frank Leboeuf anchoring the defence. He is expected to return from injury for Sunday's match. Gullit is a staunch advocate of what he likes to call "sexy football". Chelsea play short passes to feet, aiming to release Gianfranco Zola or Gianluca Vialli through the channels. Mark Hughes adds a touch of Welsh grit just behind either of the two Italians.

Strengths: Individual players capable of turning a match. Zola has been a revelation since his arrival from Parma in November. Vialli shone early in the season and although he has often been relegated to the bench since then he is still potentially devastating. Hughes is as combative as ever and Lebouef and Di Matteo ensure class is not limited to Chelsea's front line.

Weaknesses: Chelsea's midfielders and defenders -- Leboeuf and di Matteo excepted -- are not of the same calibre as their forwards. They have never settled on a first-choice goalkeeper and both Frode Grodas and Kevin Hitchcock are inconsistent.

Motivation: Chelsea are the arch-underachievers of English football and know it is high time they won trophies rather than simply praise for their style of play. They will want to make up for the disappointment of defeat in last year's semifinal and the 1994 final. Revenge for Wimbledon's 4-2 victory in their league clash at Stamford Bridge early this season.
Team (probable): Frode Grodas, Franck Leboeuf, Steve Clarke, Frank Sinclair, Craig Burley, Roberto Di Matteo, Scott Minto, Dennis Wise, Eddy Newton, Mark Hughes, Gainfranco Zola.

Playing style: Wimbledon are no longer the kick-and-rush side of the 1980s and have played some of their neatest football this season. A basic 4-4-2 formation. They still rely on the strength and height of Marcus Gayle and Efan Ekoku up front but their build-up play and crossing has been improved by Norwegian Oyvind Leonhardson and Neal Ardley on the flanks. Midfielder Vinnie Jones, centre-back Chris Perry and goalkeeper Neil Sullivan form a solid backbone to the side.

Strengths: The traditional attributes of a British club side -- physical strength, team work and a never-say-die spirit. Ekoku, Gayle and Robbie Earle are a handful for any defence and Neil Sullivan is one of the safest goalkeepers in the premier league.
Weaknesses: No single player of the calibre of Zola, Di Matteo or Gullit to turn a game on its head with a piece of individual skill.

Motivation: Wimbledon, known as "the academy of team spirit", are always motivated. Knocked out of the League Cup in the semifinals, they will not want a repeat in the F.A. Cup. A place in the UEFA cup via the league is slipping out of sight and this remains their only realistic chance of qualifying for Europe. Revenge for last season's sixth round defeat by Chelsea.
Team (probable): Neil Sullivan, Alan Kimble, Chris Perry, Brian McAllister, Vinnie Jones, Peter Fear, Neal Ardley, Oyvind Leonhardson, Robbie Earle, Marcus Gayle, Efan Ekoku.
